1:1: And Adonoy spoke to Moshe in the Sinai desert, in the Tent of Meeting, on the first [day] of the second month, in the second year of their exodus from the land of Egypt, saying:

AND the Lord spake with Mosheh in the wilderness of Sinai, in the tabernacle of ordinance, on the first of the month Ijar, which was the second month of the second year from the time of their coming forth from the land of Mizraim, saying:
1:2: Take a head count [the sum] of the entire congregation of Bnei Yisroel according to their families to the house of their fathers counting the names of all males individually.
Take the account of the whole congregation of the Beni Israel, according to the families of their fathers' house, by the number of the names of all the males by their capitations.
1:3: From twenty years old and above, all those eligible for the army [who go to war] of Israel, you shall count them according to their divisions, you and Aharon.
From each son twenty years and upwards, every one going out in the host in Israel; thou and Aharon number them by their hosts.
1:4: Along with you, there shall be one man for each tribe, each man shall be the head of his fathers’ house.
And let there be with you a man of each tribe, a chief of his father's house.
1:5: These are the names of the men who shall stand along with you. For [the tribe of] Reuven, Elitzur the son of Shdeiur.
And these are the names of the men who shall stand with you. Of Reuben, Elizur bar Shedeur:
1:6: For [the tribe of] Shimon, Shlumiel the son of Tzurishadai.
of Shemeon, the leader, Shelumiel bar Zuri-Shaddai:
1:7: For [the tribe of] Yehudah, Nachshon the son of Aminadav.
the prince of Jehudah, Nachshon bar Amminadab:
1:8: For [the tribe of] Yissachar, Nesanel the son of Tzu’ar.
the prince of Issakar, Nathaniel bar Zuar:
1:9: For [the tribe of] Zevulun, Eliav the son of Cheilon.
the prince of Zebulon, Eliab bar Chelon:
1:10: For the sons of Yoseif, for [the tribe of] Ephraim, Elishamah the son of Amihud. For [the tribe of] Menasheh, Gamliel the son of Pedahtzur.
the prince of the Beni Joseph, of Ephraim, Elishama bar Ammihud: the prince of Menasheh, Gamliel bar Pedazur:
1:11: For [the tribe of] Binyamin, Avidan the son of Gid’oni.
the prince of Benjamin, Abidan bar Gideoni:
1:12: For [the tribe of] Don, Achiezer the son of Amishadai.
the prince of Dan, Achiezer bar Ammi-shadai:
1:13: For [the tribe of] Asher, Pagi’el the son of Ochran.
the prince of Asher, Pagiel bar Achran:
1:14: For [the tribe of] Gad, Elyasaf the son of De’uel.
the prince of Gad, Eljasaph bar Dehuel:
1:15: For [the tribe of] Naftali, Achira the son of Einan.
the prince of Naphtali, Achira bar Enan.
1:16: These are the ones called from the congregation, the leaders of their fathers’ tribes; they are the heads of the thousands of Yisroel.
These (were) the notables of the congregation of the people, chiefs of their fathers' tribes, heads of thousands in Israel these.
1:17: Moshe and Aharon took these men who were designated by name.
And Mosheh and Aharon took these men who are expressed by their names:
1:18: They gathered together the entire congregation on the first [day] of the second month and they were registered by family ancestry according to the house of their fathers. according to the number of names each man of twenty years and above; individually.

and they assembled all the congregation on the first day of the month Ijar, which is the second month, and recensed them by the families of their fathers' house, by the number of their names, from twenty years old and upward by their capitations.
1:19: Just as Adonoy commanded Moshe. He counted them in the Sinai desert.
As the Lord commanded Mosheh, they numbered them in the wilderness of Sinai.
1:20: These were the sons of Reuven, Yisroel’s firstborn, their births according to their families according to the house of their fathers. according to the number of individual names every male of twenty years and above, all who go forth into the army.

And the sons of Reuben, the first-born of Israel by the families of the generations of their fathers' house, in the number of their names by their polls, every male from twenty years old and upward, all going forth in the host,
1:21: Their nunbers, for the tribe of Reuven, is forty-six thousand five hundred.
the sum of the tribe of Reuben, forty-six thousand Five hundred.
1:22: For the sons of Shimon, their births according to their families according to the house of their fathers, his numbers according to the number of individual names every male of twenty years and above, all who go forth into the army.

Of the families of the Beni Shemeon, after the generations of their fathers' house in the number of their names by their polls, every male from twenty years and upward, every one going forth in the host,
1:23: Their numbers, for the tribe of Shimon, is fifty-nine thousand three hundred.
the sum of the tribe of Shemeon, fifty-nine thousand three hundred:
1:24: For the sons of Gad, their births according to their families according to the house of their fathers in a counting of names. From twenty years and above, all who go forth into the army.
of the family of the Beni Gad, after the generation of their fathers' house, in the number of their names by their polls, every male from twenty years and upward,
1:25: Their numbers, for the tribe of Gad, is forty-five thousand six hundred and fifty.
the sum of the tribe of Dan, forty-five thousand six hundred and fifty.
1:26: For the sons of Yehudah, their births according to their families according to the house of their fathers, in a counting of names. From twenty years and above, all who go forth into the army.
of the family of the Beni Jehudah, after the generation of their fathers' house, in the number of their names by their polls, every male from twenty years and upward,
1:27: Their numbers, for the tribe of Yehudah, is seventy-four thousand six hundred.
The sum of the tribe of Jehudah seventy-four thousand six hundred:
1:28: For the sons of Yissachar, their births according to their families according to the house of their fathers, in a counting of names. From twenty years and above, all who go forth into the army.
of the family of the Beni Issakar, after the generation of their fathers' house, in the number of their names by their polls, every male from twenty years and upward,
1:29: Their numbers, for the tribe of Yissachar is fifty-four thousand four hundred.
The sum of the tribe of Issakar, fifty-four thousand four hundred:
1:30: For the sons of Zevulun, their births according to their families according to the house of their fathers, in a counting of names from twenty years and above, all who go forth into the army.
of the family of the Beni Zebulon, after the generation of their fathers' house, in the number of their names by their polls, every male from twenty years and upward,
1:31: Their numbers, for the tribe of Zevulun, is fifty-seven thousand four hundred.
The sum of the tribe of Zebulon, fifty-seven thousand four hundred:
1:32: For the sons of Yoseif; For the sons of Ephraim their births according to their families according to the house of their fathers, in a counting of names from twenty years and above, all who go forth into the army.
of the family of the Beni Joseph of the family of the Beni Ephraim, after the generation of their fathers' house, in the number of their names by their polls, every male from twenty years and upward,
1:33: Their numbers, for the tribe of Ephraim is forty thousand five hundred.
The sum of the tribe of Ephraim, forty thousand five hundred:
1:34: For the sons of Menashe, their births according to their families according to the house of their fathers, in a counting of names from twenty years and above, all who go forth into the army.
of the family of the Beni Menasheh, after the generation of their fathers' house, in the number of their names by their polls, every male from twenty years and upward,
1:35: Their numbers, for the tribe of Menashe is thirty-two thousand two hundred.
The sum of the tribe of Menasheh, thirty-two thousand two hundred:
1:36: For the sons of Binyamin, their births according to their families according to the house of their fathers, in a counting of names from twenty years and above, all who go forth into the army.
of the family of the Beni Benjamin, after the generation of their fathers' house, in the number of their names by their polls, every male from twenty years and upward,
1:37: Their numbers for the tribe of Binyamin, is thirty-five thousand four hundred.
The sum of the tribe of Benjamin, thirty five thousand four hundred:
1:38: For the sons of Don, their births according to their families according to the house of their fathers, in a counting of names from twenty years and above, all who go forth into the army.
of the family of the Beni Dan, after the generation of their fathers' house, in the number of their names by their polls, every male from twenty years and upward,
1:39: Their numbers, for the tribe of Don, is sixty-two thousand seven hundred.
The sum of the tribe of Dan, sixty-two thousand seven hundred:
1:40: For the sons of Asher, their births according to their families according to the house of their fathers, in a counting of names from twenty years and above, all who go forth into the army.
of the family of the Beni Asher, after the generation of their fathers' house, in the number of their names by their polls, every male from twenty years and upward,
1:41: Their numbers, for the tribe of Asher is forty-one thousand five hundred.
The sum of the tribe of Asher, forty-one thousand five hundred:
1:42: The sons of Naftali, their births according to their families according to the house of their fathers, in a counting of names from twenty years and above, all who go forth into the army.
of the family of the Beni Naphtali, after the generation of their fathers' house, in the number of their names by their polls, every male from twenty years and upward,
1:43: Their numbers, for the tribe of Naftali is fifty-three thousand four hundred.
The sum of the tribe of Naphtali, fifty-three thousand four hundred.
1:44: These are the numbers which were counted [by] Moshe, Aharon and the leaders of Israel, [being] twelve men, each man was the head of his fathers’ house.
These are the sums of the numbered ones which Mosheh and Aharon, and the princes of Israel, twelve men, a man for each house of their fathers, did number.
1:45: All the numbers of Bnei Yisroel according to the house of their fathers, from twenty years and above, all who go forth into the army of Israel,
1:46: All their numbers were six hundred and three thousand five hundred and fifty.
And all the sums (of the numbered of the Beni Israel) were six hundred and three thousand five hundred and fifty.
1:47: The Levites, according to the tribe of their fathers were not counted among them.
But the Levites after their father's tribe were not numbered among them.
1:48: For the Lord had spoken with Mosheh, saying:
1:49: However, the tribe of Levi you shall not count and you shall not take [accept] their head count among Bnei Yisroel.
Nevertheless, the tribe of Levi thou shalt not number, nor take their sum among the children of Israel:
1:50: You shall appoint the Levites to oversee the Mishkon of Testimony and over all of its utensils and over all that belongs to it. They shall carry the Mishkon and all its utensils, and they shall administer it, and they shall camp around the Mishkon.

but thou shalt appoint the Levites over the tabernacle of the testimony, and over all its vessels, and whatever things pertain unto it. They shall carry the tabernacle and all its vessels, and do service in it; and round about the tabernacle shall they dwell.
1:51: When the Mishkon is to be moved the Levites shall take it down, and when the Mishkon is to rest [in one place] the Levites shall erect it, and the stranger who approaches, shall die.

And when the tabernacle is to go forward, the Levites shall take it apart; and when the tabernacle is to be stationary, the Levites are to uprear it: the common person who draweth near will be slain by a flaming fire from before the Lord.
1:52: Bnei Yisroel shall camp, each man at his own camp and each man at his own banner, according to their divisions.
And the sons of Israel shall encamp every one by the place of his own company, every one under his standard according to their hosts.
1:53: The Levites shall camp around the Mishkon of the Testimony, so that there will not be anger upon the congregation of Bnei Yisroel, and the Levites shall be careful to preserve the Mishkon of Testimony.

But the Levites shall encamp round about the tabernacle of the testimony, that there may not be wrath upon the congregation of the children of Israel; and the Levites shall keep charge of the tabernacle of testimony.
1:54: Bnei Yisroel did according to all that Adonoy commanded Moshe; they did it [exactly].
And the sons of Israel did according to all that the Lord commanded Mosheh, so did they.
2:1: Adonoy spoke to Moshe and to Aharon, saying;
And the Lord spake with Mosheh and with Aharon, saying:
2:2: Each man at his own banner, with the insignia of their fathers’ houses shall Bnei Yisroel encamp, at a distance around the Tent of Meeting they shall encamp.

Every man of the Beni Israel shall encamp by his standard, by the ensign which is signified upon the standards of their fathers' house over against the tabernacle of ordinance shall they encamp round about.
2:3: Those whose camp is in the forefront, on the eastern side is the camp of the banner of Yehudah according to their divisions, and the leader of the sons of Yehudah is Nachshon the son of Aminadav.

The length of the camp of Israel shall be twelve miles, and its breadth twelve miles. And they who encamp eastward to the sunrise shall be of the standard of the camp of Jehudah by their hosts, spreading over four miles. And his standard shall be of silk, of three colours, corresponding with (those of) the precious stones which are in the breastplate,--sardius, topaz, and carbuncle; and upon it shall be expressed and set forth the names of the three tribes of Jehudah, Issakar, and Zebulon; and in the midst shall be written : Arise, O Lord, and let Thine enemies be scattered, and Thine adversaries be driven away before Thee; and upon it shall be set forth the figure of a young lion. And the Rabba of the Beni Jehudah shall be Nachshon bar Amminadab.
2:4: Its division and their numbers is seventy-four thousand six hundred.
And the sum of the hosts of that tribe was seventy-four thousand six hundred.
2:5: Those who camp along with [near] him are; the tribe of Yissachar, and the leader of the sons of Yissachar is Nesanel the son of Tzu’ar.
And they who encamp next by him shall be the tribe of Issakar, and the Rabba appointed over the host of the Beni Issakar, Nathaniel bar Zuar:
2:6: Its division and its numbers is fifty-four thousand four hundred.
and the sum of the host of the tribe fifty-four thousand four hundred.
2:7: The tribe of Zevulun, and the leader of the sons of Zevulun is Eliav the son of Cheilon.
The tribe of Zebulon,--the Rabba, Eliab bar Chelon;
2:8: Its division and its numbers is fifty-seven thousand four hundred.
the number, fifty-seven thousand four hundred.
2:9: The total numbers for the encampment of Yehudah is one hundred eighty-six thousand four hundred according to their divisions, [and] they travel [in the] first [position].
All the numbered ones of the camp of Jehudah, one hundred and eighty-six thousand four hundred, by their hosts; they shall go forward in front.
2:10: The banner of the camp of Reuven is on the south side, according to their divisions, and the leader of the sons of Reuven is Elitzur the son of Shdeiur.

(By) the standard of the camp of Reuben they, shall encamp southward by their hosts, spreading over four miles. And his standard shall be of silk, of three colours, corresponding with (those of) the precious stones that are in the breastplate, azmorad, sapphire, and adamant: on it shall be expressed and set forth the names of the three tribes of Reuben, Shemeon, Gad; and in the midst of it be written, Hear, Israel, the Lord our God is One; and upon it shall be set forth the figure of a stag. Some would have thought there should have been upon it the figure of a young ox; but Mosheh the prophet altered it, that the sin of the calf might not be remembered against them. And the Rabba set over the host of the tribe Reuben was Elizur bar Shedeur.
2:11: Its divisions and its numbers is forty-six thousand five hundred.
And his host and the numbered of his tribe ___
2:12: Those who camp along with him are; the tribe of Shimon, and the leader of the tribe of Shimon is Shlumiel the son of Tzurishadai.
2:13: Its division and their numbers is fifty-nine thousand three hundred;
2:14: The tribe of Gad, and the leader of the sons of Gad is Elyasaf the son of Re’uel.
The tribe of Gad: the Rabba set over the host of the tribe of the Beni Gad was Eljasaph bar Dehuel.
2:15: Its division and their numbers is forty-five thousand six hundred fifty.
And his host and the number of his tribe, forty-five thousand six hundred.
2:16: The total numbers for the encampment of Reuven is one hundred fifty-one thousand four hundred and fifty, according to their division, and they travel [in the] second [position].
All the sum of the numbered ones of the camp of Reuben, one hundred and fifty one thousand four hundred and fifty by their hosts; and they went forward secondly,
2:17: The Tent of Meeting shall travel [along with] the camp of the Levites in the center of the [other] camps, just as they camp so shall they travel, each man in his place according to their [various] banners.

But the tabernacle shall go with the host of the Levites, in the midst of their host; and their camp spreadeth over four miles, in the midst are they to be: as they encamp, so shall they go, every man going in his appointed place, by their standard.
2:18: The banner of the camp of Ephraim, according to their divisions is on the west side, and the leader of the sons of Ephraim is Elishamah the son of Amihud.

The camp of Ephraim by the standard of their hosts shall pitch on the west; their camp spreadeth over four miles; and their standard is of silk of three colours, corresponding with the precious stones in the breastplate, ligure, agate, and amethyst; and upon it expressed and set forth the names of the three tribes, Ephraim, Menasheh and Benjamin, having written in the midst, And the Cloud of the Lord was over them, in the going forward of the host; and upon it was set forth the figure of a young man. And the Rabba set over the tribe of Ephraim, Elishama bar Ammihud;
2:19: Its division and their numbers is forty-thousand five hundred.
and the sum of his host, forty thousand five hundred.
2:20: Along with [near] him are; the tribe of Menashe, and the leader of the sons of Menashe is Gamliel the son of Pedahtzur.
And next to him were the tribe of Menasheh: the Rabba, Gamliel bar Pedashur;
2:21: Its division and their numbers is thirty-two thousand two hundred.
their number, thirty-two thousand two hundred.
2:22: The tribe of Binyamin, and the leader of the sons of Binyamin is Avidan the son of Gid’oni.
Of the tribe of Benjamin the Rabba was Abidan bar Gideoni,
2:23: Its division and their numbers is thirty-five thousand four hundred.
and the number of his host thirty-five thousand four hundred.
2:24: The total numbers for the camp of Ephraim is one hundred eight thousand one hundred according to their divisions, and they travel [in the] third [position].
The Sum of the camp of Ephraim was one hundred and eight thousand one hundred; and they went forward thirdly.
2:25: The banner of the camp of Don is on the north side according to their divisions, and the leader of the sons of Don is Achiezer the son of Amishadai.

The standard of the camp of Dan shall be to the north with their hosts; and the space of their camp shall spread over four miles. His standard shall be of silk of three colours, corresponding with the stones in the breastplate, chrysolite, beryl, and jasper; in it shall be expressed and set forth the names of the three tribes, Dan, Naphtali, and Asher; and upon it shall be expressed: And in his encampment shall he say, Return, O Lord, and dwell in Thy glory in the midst of the myriads of Israel; and upon it shall also be set forth the figure of a basilisk serpent. (Gen. xlix. 17.) The Rabba set over the hosts of Dan was Achiezer bar Aminishaddai,
2:26: Its division and their numbers is sixty-two thousand seven hundred.
and the number of his tribe sixty-two thousand seven hundred.
2:27: Those who camp with him are; the tribe of Asher, and the leader of the sons of Asher is Pagi’el the son of Ochran.
They who encamp next to him shall be the tribe of Asher; the Rabbi was Paghiel bar Achran,
2:28: Its divisions and their numbers is forty-one thousand five hundred.
and the numbers forty-one thousand five hundred.
2:29: The tribe of Naftali, and the leader of the sons of Naftali is Achira the son of Einan.
Of the tribe Naphtali, the Rabba, Achira bar Enan;
2:30: Its divisions and their numbers is fifty-three thousand four hundred.
and the numbers, fifty-three thousand four hundred.
2:31: The total numbers for the encampment of Don is one hundred fifty-seven thousand six hundred and they travel [in the] last [position] according to their [various] banners.
The sum of the hosts of Dan was one hundred and fifty-seven thousand six hundred: and these went forward last with their ensigns.
2:32: These are the numbers of Bnei Yisroel according to their fathers’ houses. The total numbers of the camps according to their divisions is six hundred three thousand five hundred fifty.
This is the amount of the numbers of the Beni Israel, according to the house of their fathers; all the sums of the camps by their hosts were six hundred and three thousand five hundred and fifty.
2:33: The Levites were not counted among Bnei Yisroel just as Adonoy commanded Moshe.
But the Levites were not numbered among the sons of Israel, as the Lord commanded Mosheh.
2:34: Bnei Yisroel did all which Adonoy commanded Moshe, so they camped according to their [various] banners and so they traveled, each man with his family according to his fathers’ house.
And the sons of Israel did according to all that the Lord commanded Mosheh; so did they encamp by their standards, and so went they forward, every man with his family by the house of his fathers.
3:1: These are the descendants of Aharon and Moshe on the day that Adonoy spoke to Moshe on Mount Sinai.
These are the generations of Aharon and Mosheb, who were genealogized in the day that the Lord spake with Mosheh in the mountain of Sinai.
3:2: These are the names of Aharon’s sons; the firstborn, Nadav, and Avihu, Elazar and Isamar.
3:3: These are the names of Aharon’s sons, the anointed kohanim, whose hands are occupied with bringing offerings, to serve [God].

And these are the names of the Beni Aharon the priests, the disciples of Moses, the Rabbi of Israel; and they were called by his name in the day that they were anointed to minister in offering their oblations.
3:4: Nadav and Avihu died in the presence of Adonoy, when they offered a strange fire-offering before Adonoy, in the Sinai desert, and they had no sons. [However] Elazar and Isamar served in the presence of their father Aharon.

But Nadab and Abihu died by the flaming fire at the time of their offering the strange fire from their own tents; and they had no children. And Elazar and Ithamar ministered before Aharon their father.
3:5: And the Lord spake with Mosheh, saying:
3:6: Bring the tribe of Levi near and have it stand before Aharon the kohein, and they shall serve him.
Bring the tribe of Levi near, and appoint them before Aharon the priest to minister with him, (or, to do him service;)
3:7: They shall take care to preserve his guardianship and the guardianship of the entire congregation before the Tent of Meeting, to serve in the service of the Mishkon.
and let them be divided into twenty and four parties, and they shall keep his charge, and the charge of all the congregation before the tabernacle of ordinance, to perform the work of the tabernacle;
3:8: They shall guard all the utensils of the Tent of Meeting and the watch of Bnei Yisroel to serve in the service of the Mishkon.
and they shall have charge of all the vessels of the tabernacle of ordinance, and the charge of the sons of Israel to do the service of the tabernacle.
3:9: You shall place the Levites in the charge of Aharon and his sons; they are presented [and given] to him from [among] Bnei Yisroel.
And I have given the Levites unto Aharon and his sons; a gift are they given and delivered to him from among the sons of Israel;
3:10: You shall appoint Aharon and his sons and they shall guard their priesthood, and an outsider (non-kohein) who comes near shall be put to death.
and number thou Aharon and his sons, that they may keep their priesthood; and the stranger who cometh near shall be slain by the flame from. before the Lord.
3:11: And the Lord spake with Mosheh, saying:
3:12: Behold! I have taken the Levites from among Bnei Yisroel instead of all the firstborn who have opened the womb, among Bnei Yisroel, and [therefore] the Levites shall be Mine [serve before Me].
And I, behold, I have brought nigh the Levites from among the sons of Israel, instead of all the first-born who open the womb among the sons of Israel; and the Levites shall minister before Me.
3:13: For all the firstborn are Mine, since on the day I smote all the firstborn in the land of Egypt I sanctified to [before] Me all the firstborn of Bnei Yisroel from man to beast; they shall be Mine, I am Adonoy.

For every first-born among the sons of Israel is Mine, from the day when. I slew every first-born in the land of Mizraim; I have sanctified before Me every first-born in Israel; from man to animal, they are Mine: I am the Lord.
3:14: Adonoy spoke to Moshe in the Sinai desert, saying;
And the Lord spake with Mosheh in the wilderness of Sinai, saying:
3:15: Count the sons of Levi according to their fathers’ houses according to their families. All males from the age of one month and above, you shall count them.
Number the sons of Levi according to the house of their fathers and their families; every male from a month old and upward shalt thou number them.
3:16: Moshe counted them according to the word of Adonoy, just as he was commanded.
Moses therefore numbered them according to the mouth of the Word of the Lord, as he had been commanded.
3:17: These were sons of Levi according to their names, Gershon, Kehos and Merori.
And these were the sons of Levi by their names: Gershon, Kehath, and Merari.
3:18: These are the names of Gershon’s sons according to their families; Livni and Shim’i.
And these are the names of the Beni Gershon, according to their families, Libni and Shemei.
3:19: The sons of Kehos, according to their families were; Amram, Yitzhar Chevron and Uziel.
And the Beni Kehath by their families, Amram, Jizhar, Hebron, and Uzziel.
3:20: The sons of Merori, according to their families were; Machli and Mushi. These are the families of Levi according to their fathers’ houses.
And the Beni Merari by their families, Machli, and Mushi: these are the families of the Levites after the house of their fathers.
3:21: Of Gershon, the family of Livni and the family of Shim’i. These are the families of the Gershonites.
Of Gershon, the family of Libni, and the family of Shemei; these are the families of Gershon.
3:22: Their numbers, in a count of every male of one month and above; their numbers are seven thousand five hundred.
The sum of them, by the numbers of all the males from a month old and upward, seven thousand five hundred.
3:23: The families of the Gershonites shall camp behind the Mishkon on the west side.
The two families who spring from Gershon shall encamp after the tabernacle westward;
3:24: The leader of the household of the Gershonites is Elyasaf the son of Lael.
and the Rab of the house of the fathers set over the two families shall be Eljasaph bar Lael.
3:25: The guardianship of the sons of Gershon in the Tent of Meeting [was]; the Mishkon and the Tent, its cover and the Curtain for the entrance of the Tent of Meeting,
And the charge of the Beni Gershon in the tabernacle of ordinance shall be the tent, and the covering that overspreadeth, and the hanging of the door of the tabernacle of ordinance,
3:26: The hanging Curtains of the courtyard and the Curtain at the entrance of the courtyard which is around the Mishkon and Altar, and its ropes, for all of the work involving these things [its service].
and the curtains of the court, and the hanging which is at the gate of the court by the tabernacle, and the altar round about, and the cords of it, for all the service thereof.
3:27: Of Kehos, was the family of Amram, the family of Yitzhar, the family of Chevron and the family of Uziel, these are the families of the Kehosites.
Of Kehath was the family of Amram, and the family of Izbar, and of Hebron, and Uzziel: these are the families of Kehath,
3:28: The number of every male from one month and above is eight thousand six hundred. [They were] the guardians of the sacred vessels.
the numbers eight thousand six hundred, keeping the charge of the sanctuary.
3:29: The families of the children of Kehos shall camp on the south side of the Mishkon.
The four families that spring from Kehath shall encamp by the south side of the tabernacle;
3:30: The leader of the household of the families of the Kehosites, is Elitzafan the son of Uziel.

Speak with the children of Israel, and say to them: When a man or, woman, seeing her who had gone astray in her corruption, shall (resolve to) become abstinent from wine, or for any other cause shall make the vow of a Nazir in separating one'- self unto the Name of the Lord,
6:3: From new or old [intoxicating] wine, he must abstain. Vinegar made from new wine and vinegar made from old wine he shall not drink; anything steeped in grapes he shall not drink; moist grapes or dried grapes (raisins) he shall not eat.
he shall abstain from wine, new and old, he shall drink neither vinegar of old wine or new; neither may he drink liquor in which grapes have been crushed, nor eat of grapes either fresh or dried.
6:4: As long as he is a Nazir from anything made of the grape-vine, from seeds to skin, he shall not eat.
All the days of his vow he shall not eat of the tree which maketh wine, from the husks of grapes even to the kernels within them.
6:5: As long as [all the days] he is under his nazirite oath a razor shall not pass over [to touch] his head. Until he completes his days as a Nazir to Adonoy he shall be sacred, he shall let the hair of his head grow long.

All the days of his nazir-vow the razor shall not pass upon his head until the time when the days of his separation to the Name of the Lord be fulfilled; he shall be consecrate, letting the hair of his head grow.
6:6: All the days that he is a Nazir to Adonoy, he shall have no contact with the dead.
All the days of his separation to the Name of the Lord he shall not go in where there is a dead man.
6:7: For his father, mother, brother and sister he shall not [ritually] defile himself for them when they die. For, the nazirite crown of his God is upon his head.
For his father, or his mother, his brother, or his sister, he shall not make himself unclean through their decease; for the crown of Eloah is upon his head;
6:8: All the days of his separation, he is sacred to Adonoy.
all the days in which he is a Nazir lie shall be sacred before the Lord.
6:9: If someone died near him suddenly, or unexpectedly, and caused his nazirite crowned head to be defiled, he shall shave his head on the day of his purification, he shall shave it on the seventh day.
But if a person die near him suddenly, and he unawares defile the head of his vow, let him shave his head on the day of his purification; on the seventh day let him shave it.
6:10: On the eighth day he shall take two turtledoves or two young pigeons to the kohein, to the entrance of the Tent of Meeting.
And on the eighth day let him bring two turtle doves, or two young pigeons, unto the priest at the door of the tabernacle of ordinance.
6:11: The kohein shall prepare one for a sin-offering and one for a burnt-offering and atone on his behalf from his sin [of contact] with a [departed] soul, and he shall sanctify his head on that day.

And the priest shall make one a sin offering, and one a burnt offering, and atone for him on account of that in which he hath sinned, in defiling himself by the dead: and he shall consecrate his head on that day.
6:12: He shall set apart, for Adonoy, his nazirite days, and bring a sheep in its first year as a guilt-offering. The first days shall elapse because his nazirite crown was defiled.

And let him dedicate before the Lord the days of his nazirate (afresh), and bring a lamb of the year for a trespass offering; but the former days will have been in vain, because he had defiled his nazirate.
6:13: This is the law of the Nazir: when the days of his nazirite status are fulfilled, he shall bring himself to the entrance of the Tent of Meeting.
And this is the law of the Nazir on the day when his separation days are fulfilled: Let him present himself at the door of the tabernacle of ordinance,
6:14: He shall bring his offering to Adonoy; one unblemished sheep, in its first year, as a burnt-offering, and one unblemished ewe, in its first year as a sin-offering, and one unblemished ram as a peace-offering [sacred sacrifice].

and bring his oblation before the Lord, one lamb of the year unblemished for a burnt offering, and one ewe Iamb of the year unblemished for a sin offering, and one ram unblemished for the consecrated oblation;
6:15: A basket of matzos of fine flour, loaves mixed with oil and matzoh-wafers spread with oil and their meal-offerings and libations.
and a basket of unleavened cakes of flour with olive oil, and unleavened wafers anointed with olive oil, their minchas and libations.
6:16: The kohein shall bring it before Adonoy and do the service of his sin-offering and of his burnt-offering.
And the priest shall offer before the Lord, and perform the sin offering, and the burnt sacrifice;
6:17: He shall make the ram a peace-offering [sacred sacrifice] for Adonoy along with the basket of matzos, and the kohein shall do the service of his meal-offering and libation.
and make the ram a consecrated victim (peace offering) before the Lord, with the basket of unleavened; and the priest shall make its mincha and its libation.
6:18: The Nazir shall shave—at the entrance to the Tent of Meeting—the nazirite crown of hair on his head, and he shall take the hair from the nazirite crown on his head and put it in the fire which is under the [cauldron of the] peace-offering [sacred] sacrifice.

And the Nazir shall shave his consecrated head, without, after the offering of the holy oblations at the door of the tabernacle of ordinance, and take the hair of his consecrated head, and lay it on the fire that is under the cauldron of the peace offering.
6:19: The kohein shall take the cooked foreleg from the ram and one matzoh-loaf from the basket, and one matzoh-wafer, and put it on the palms [hands] of the Nazir after he has shaved his nazirite crown.

And the priest shall take the shoulder that is boiled, entire from the ram, and one unleavened cake from the basket, and one unleavened wafer, and put upon the hands of the Nazirite, after he hath shaved his head of the consecration.
6:20: The kohein shall wave them as a wave-offering, before Adonoy. It is consecrated to the kohein besides the breast of the wave-offering and the separated thigh portion. After this, the Nazir may drink wine.
And the priest shall uplift them for an elevation. It is sacred; it belongeth to the priest, with the breast of the elevation, and the separated shoulder. And after that the Nazirite may drink wine.
6:21: This is the law of the Nazir who has vowed—[this is] his offering to Adonoy for his nazirite vow, aside from what he can afford [lit. may attach to his hands] to bring according to his vow that he vows. So shall he fulfill in addition to the laws of his nazirite [vows.]

This is the declaration of the law of the Nazir who shall have vowed his oblation before the Lord for his separation, besides what may come into his hand according to the rule (or measure) of his vow, to bring that which he had vowed; so shall he do according to the law of his nazirate.
6:22: And the Lord spake with Mosheh, saying:
6:23: Speak to Aharon and to his sons, saying; This is how you shall bless Bnei Yisroel, saying to them:
Speak with Aharon and his sons, saying: Thus shall you bless the children of Israel, while spreading forth the hands from the high place; in this tongue.
6:24: May Adonoy bless you and protect you.

The Lord bless thee and keep thee. The Lord make His face to shine upon thee, and gracious unto thee. The Lord lift up His countenance upon thee, and grant thee peace. The Lord bless thee in all thy business, and keep) thee from demonsof the night, and things that cause terror, and from demons of the noon and of the morning, and from malignant spirits and phantoms.
6:25: May Adonoy cause His countenance [Shechinah] to shine upon you and favor you.
The Lord make His face to shine upon thee, when occupied in the law, and reveal to thee its secrets, and be merciful unto thee.
6:26: May Adonoy lift His face to you, and grant you peace.
The Lord lift up His countenance upon thee in thy prayer, and grant thee peace in thy end.
6:27: They shall bestow [the blessing of] My Name upon Bnei Yisroel, and I will bless them.
And they shall bestow the benediction of My Name upon the children of Israel, and I, by My Word, will bless them.
7:1: It came to pass, on the day Moshe finished erecting the Mishkon, and he anointed it and consecrated it and all of its utensils, and the Altar and all its utensils, and he anointed them and consecrated them.

And it was on the day which begins the month of Nisan, when Mosheh had finished to uprear the tabernacle, he took it not in pieces again, but anointed and consecrated it and all its vessels, the altar and all the vessels thereof, and he anointed them and hallowed them;
7:2: The leaders of Israel brought, [those who were] the heads of their fathers’ houses; they were the leaders of the tribes, they stood by during the counting.
then the leaders of Israel, who were the chiefs of the house of their fathers, brought their offerings. These were they who had been appointed in Mizraim chiefs over the numbered,
7:3: They brought their offerings before Adonoy; six covered wagons and twelve oxen; a wagon for each two leaders and an ox for each individual, and they placed them before the Mishkon.

and they brought their offering before the Lord; six wagons covered and fitted up, and twelve oxen; one wagon for two princes and one ox for each. But Mosheh was not willing to receive them, and they brought them before the tabernacle.
7:4: And the Lord spake with Mosheh, saying:
7:5: Take [the offering] from them, and let them be used for the service of the Tent of Meeting. Give them to the Levites, each man according to [the needs] his work.

Take them, and let them be used for the need of the appointed (work), and let the oxen and the wagons be for the work of the service of the tabernacle of ordinance, and give them to the Levites, to each according to the measure of his work.
7:6: Moshe took the wagons and the oxen and gave them to the Levites.
And Mosheh took the wagons and the oxen, and gave them to the Levites.
7:7: Two [of the] wagons and four [of the] oxen he gave to the sons of Gershon, according to [the needs] their work.
Two wagons and four oxen he gave to the sons of Gershon, according to the amount of their service,
7:8: Four [of the] wagons and eight [of the] oxen he gave to the sons of Merori. According to their work they were in the charge of Isamar the son of Aharon the kohein.
and four wagons and eight oxen gave be to the sons of Merari, according to the measure of their service, by the hand of Ithamar bar Aharon the priest.
7:9: He did not give any to the sons of Kehos because the sacred work was [incumbent] upon them, which they had to carry on their shoulders.
But to the sons of Kehath he gave neither wagons nor oxen, because on them was laid the service of the sanctuary, to be carried on their shoulders.
7:10: The leaders brought forward the [offerings for] the consecration of the altar on the day it was anointed. The leaders placed their offering before the altar.
And the princes offered at the dedication of the altar by anointing, on the day that he anointed it did the princes present their oblations before the altar.
7:11: Adonoy said to Moshe: One leader each day, one leader each day, they shall bring forth their offering, for the dedication of the altar.
And the Lord said unto Mosheh, Let the princes offer each, one prince on one day, their oblations at the dedication of the altar by anointing.
7:12: The one that brought his offering on the first day [was] Nachshon the son of Aminadav, of the tribe of Yehudah.
He who on the first day presented his oblation was Nachshon bar Amminadab, prince of the house of the fathers of the tribe Jehudah:
7:13: His offering was one silver tray, its weight was one hundred thirty shekolim; one silver bowl [that weighed] seventy shekolim according to sanctuary weights. Both were filled with fine flour kneaded with [olive] oil, for a meal-offering.

and his oblation which he offered was one silver bowl, thickly embossed, (or, crusted,) in weight one hundred and thirty shekels, in shekels of the sanctuary; one silver vase, slightly embossed, of seventy shekels, in shekels of the sanctuary; both of these vessels he brought filled with flour of the separation, sprinkled with olive oil for a mincha;
7:14: One spoon of ten gold [shekolim], filled with [fragrant] incense.
one pan (censer) weighing ten silver shekels, but it was itself of good gold; and he brought it full of good sweet incense of the separation;
7:15: One young bull, one ram, and one yearling sheep for a burnt-offering.
one young bullock of three years, one ram of two years, and one lamb of the year. These three did the chief of the tribe Jehudah bring for a burnt offering;
7:16: one kid of the goats he brought for a sin offering;
7:17: For the peace [sacred]-offering, two oxen, five rams, five kids, and five yearling sheep. This was the offering of Nachshon the son of Aminadav.
and for consecrated victims, two oxen, five rams, five goats, lambs of the year five: this is the order of the oblation which Nachshon bar Amminadab offered of his wealth.
7:18: On the second day, [he that] brought [was] Nesanel the son of Tzu’ar, the leader of Yissachar.

7:84: This was the dedication of the altar on the day that it was anointed, given by the leaders of Israel; twelve silver trays twelve silver bowls and twelve golden spoons.

This is the oblation at the anointing of the altar, on the day that they anointed it, from the riches of the princes of Israel: twelve silver bowls, answering to the twelve tribes; twelve silver vases, answering to the twelve princes of the Beni Israel; twelve golden pans, answering to the twelve signs (mazalia).
7:85: One hundred thirty [shekolim was the weight of] each silver tray and each bowl weighed seventy [shekolim]. All the silver vessels weighed two thousand four hundred [shekolim] according to sanctuary weights.

One hundred and thirty shekels was the weight of each silver bowl, answering to the years of Jokebed when she bare Mosheh; and seventy shekels was the weight of each vase, answering to the seventy elders of the great Sanhedrin: all the silver vessels, two thousand four hundred shekels, in shekels of the sanctuary.
7:86: Twelve golden spoons filled with [fragrant] incense; each spoon weighed ten [shekolim] according to sanctuary weights. The total of the golden spoons is one hundred twenty [shekolim].

The golden pans were twelve, answering to the princes of Israel, full of good sweet incense; the weight of ten shekels was the weight of each pan, answering to the Ten Words; all the gold of the pans, one hundred and and twenty (shekels), answering to the years lived by Mosheh the prophet.
7:87: The total of the oxen for the burnt-offering is twelve oxen, twelve rams, twelve yearling sheep and their meal-offerings, and twelve he-goats for a sin-offering.

All the bullocks for the burnt offering, twelve, a bullock for a prince of the house of the fathers; twelve rams, because the twelve princes of Ishmael would perish; twelve lambs of the year, because the twelve princes of Persia would perish; and their minchas, that famine might be removed from the world; and twelve kids of the goats for the sin offering, to atone for the sins of the twelve tribes.
7:88: The total of the oxen for the peace [sacred]-offering sacrifice is twenty-four oxen, sixty rams, sixty kids and sixty yearling sheep. This was the dedication of the altar after it was anointed.

And all the oxen for consecrated victims, twenty-four, answering to the twenty-four orders (of the priests); the rams, sixty, answering, to the sixty years which Izhak had lived when he begat Jakob; the goats, sixty, answering to the sixty letters in the benediction of the priests; lambs of the year, sixty, to atone for the sixty myriads of Israel. This was the dedication of the altar by anointment on the day that they anointed it.
7:89: When Moshe would enter the Tent of Meeting to speak with Him (God), he would hear the Voice being spoken to him from above the Ark-cover which is atop the Ark of the Testimony from between the two cherubim; and He spoke to him.

And when Mosheh entered into the tabernacle of ordinance to speak with Him, he heard the voice of the Spirit who spake with him descending from the heaven of heavens upon the Mercy Seat which was upon the Ark of the Testimony between the two Cherubim, and from thence was the Oracle {Word; Dibbera} speaking with him.
8:1: And Adonoy spoke to Moshe, saying;
And the Lord spake with Mosheh, saying:
8:2: Speak to Aharon, and say to him; When you light the lamps towards the face of the Menorah shall the seven lamps cast [their] light.

Speak with Aharon, and say to him: At the time when thou dost kindle the lamps upon the candelabrum, (all) the seven lamps shall be alight; three on the western side, and three on the eastern side, and the seventh in the midst.
8:3: Aharon did so; towards the face of the Menorah he lit its lamps, just as Adonoy commanded Moshe.
And Aharon did so; at the face of the candelabrum he lit the lamps thereof, as the Lord commanded Mosheh.
8:4: This is how the Menorah was made; beaten from [a block of] gold, from its base until its flowers it is beaten out [of a solid block], according to the vision which Adonoy showed to Moshe, so he made the Menorah.

And this was the work of the candelabrum, which was of beaten gold, from its foundations unto its lilies, the work of the artificer, with the hammer was it wrought: according to the vision which the Lord had showed Mosheh, so did Bezalel make the candelabrum.
8:5: And the Lord spake with Mosheh, saying:
8:6: Take [bring near] the Levites from among Bnei Yisroel and purify them.
Bring the Levites out from among the sons of Israel, and purify them.
8:7: This is what you shall do to them, to purify them; sprinkle them with the sin-offering waters, and cause a razor to pass over (shave) their entire bodies, and they shall wash their garments and purify themselves.

And this shalt thou do to purify them. Sprinkle upon them the water for uncleanness through sin (chattatha), and let the razor pass over all their flesh, and let them wash their raiment, and wash themselves in forty savan of water.
8:8: They should take a young bullock and its meal-offering of flour mixed with oil, and you shall take a second young bullock, for a sin-offering.
And they shall take a young bullock, and his mincha of flour sprinkled with olive oil; and take thou a second young bullock for a sin offering.
8:9: You shall bring the Levites near, before the Tent of Meeting, and you shall gather the entire congregation of Bnei Yisroel.
And thou shalt bring the Levites before the tabernacle of ordinance, and gather together also all the congregation of the sons of Israel.
8:10: You shall bring the Levites near, before Adonoy, and Bnei Yisroel shall lay their hands on the Levites.
Thou shalt bring the Levites before the Lord, and the sons of Israel shall lay their hands upon the Levites.
8:11: Aharon shall wave the Levites as a wave-offering before Adonoy from Bnei Yisroel and they will be [entrusted] to do the worship of Adonoy.
And Aharon shall present the Levites, (as) an elevation before the Lord from the sons of Israel, and they shall be for the work of the service of the Lord.
8:12: The Levites shall lay their hands on the head of the bulls and make the one for a sin-offering and the [other] one for a burnt-offering to Adonoy, to atone for the Levites.
And the Levites shall lay their hands upon the head of the bullocks, and make one a sin offering and one a burnt offering before the Lord, to atone for the Levites.
8:13: You shall set the Levites before Aharon and before his sons, and lift them up as a wave-offering to Adonoy.
And thou shalt place the Levites before Aharon and his sons, and present them (as) an elevation before the Lord;
8:14: You shall separate the Levites from among Bnei Yisroel and the Levites shall be Mine [serve before Me].
and thus shalt thou separate the Levites from among the sons of Israel, that the Levites may be ministers before Me.
8:15: After this is done, the Levites shall come to work in the Tent of Meeting, and you shall purify them, and you shall lift them up as a wave-offering,
And afterward the Levites may enter to fulfil the service of the tabernacle of ordinance, when thou shalt have purified them and presented them (as) an elevation;
8:16: For they are given [have been separated]; they are given [have been separated] to Me from among Bnei Yisroel in place of those who open the womb,—every firstborn of Bnei Yisroel—I have taken them to be Mine.
for separated they are separate before Me from among the sons of Israel, instead of every one who openeth the womb; the first-born of all who are of the sons of Israel have I taken (to be) before Me.
8:17: For every firstborn of Bnei Yisroel is Mine, human and animal; on the day in which I slew every firstborn in the land of Egypt, I have sanctified them to be Mine.
For every first-born of the sons of Israel is Mine, whether of man or of beast: in the day that I slew all the first-born in the land of Mizraim, I sanctified them before Me;
8:18: I have taken the Levites instead of all firstborn of Bnei Yisroel,
and I have taken the Levites instead of all the first-born of the sons of Israel,
8:19: and I have given the Levites to be given as a gift to Aharon and to his sons from among Bnei Yisroel to do the duties of Bnei Yisroel in the Tent of Meeting, and to atone for Bnei Yisroel, so that there will not be a plague among Bnei Yisroel when Bnei Yisroel approach the sanctuary.

and have given the Levites (as) gifts unto Aharon and to his sons from among the sons of Israel, to minister the service of the children of Israel in the tabernacle of ordinance, and to atone for the children of Israel, lest there be mortality among the children of Israel at the time when they approach the sanctuary.
8:20: Moshe, Aharon, and the entire congregation of Bnei Yisroel did to the Levites just as Adonoy commanded Moshe regarding the Levites, so did Bnei Yisroel do to them.
And Mosheh and Aharon and all the congregation of the Beni Israel did unto the Levites according to all that the Lord had commanded Mosheh concerning the Levites, so did the sons of Israel to them.
8:21: The Levites underwent purification and they washed their garments, and Aharon lifted them as a wave-offering before Adonoy; and Aharon achieved atonement on their behalf, to purify them.
And the Levites were purified, and they washed their raiment; and Aharon presented them as an elevation before the Lord. And Aharon made atonement for them to purify them.
8:22: Afterwards, the Levites came to perform their duties in the Tent of Meeting in the presence of Aharon and in the presence of his sons; just as Adonoy commanded Moshe regarding the Levites, so they did unto them.
And afterward the Levites went in to fulfil their ministry in the tabernacle of ordinance, before Aharon and his sons: as the Lord had commanded Mosheh concerning the Levites, so did they unto them.
8:23: And the Lord spake with Mosheh, saying:
8:24: This concerns the Levites; from the age of twenty-five years and above he shall enter the division for the duties of the Tent of Meeting.

This is the instruction for the Levites who are not disqualified (profaned) by their blemishes: from one of twenty-five years and upward, he shall come, according to his company, to the service of the tabernacle of ordinance
8:25: From the age of fifty he shall retire from the work force, and shall no longer work.
and from fifty years of age he shall return from the band of the service, and serve no more.
8:26: But shall serve with his brethren in the Tent of Meeting to keep the watch, and he shall not do any service; so you shall have the Levites do in their guard duties.
Yet he may minister with his brethren at the tabernacle of ordinance in keeping the watch; but he shall not do any of the service. So shall the Levites act in their charge.
9:1: Adonoy spoke to Moshe in the desert of Sinai in the second year of their exodus from the land of Egypt, in the first month, saying;
And the Lord spake with Mosheh in the wilderness of Sinai, in the second year from the time of their going forth from the land of Mizraim, in the first month, saying:
9:2: Bnei Yisroel shall perform the Pesach-offering in its proper time.
Let the children of Israel perform the sacrifice of the Pascha between the suns at its time.
9:3: On the fourteenth day of this month, in the afternoon, you shall perform it in its proper time; according to all its statutes and according to all its laws [that are appropriate for it] you shall perform it.
On the fourteenth day of this mouth, between the suns, they shall perform it in its time; according to all its rites and all its statutes shall they do it.
9:4: Moshe spoke to Bnei Yisroel [telling them] to perform the Pesach-offering.
And Mosheh spake with the children of Israel to perform the sacrifice of the Pascha.
9:5: They performed the Pesach-offering in the first [month] [in Nissan] on the fourteenth day of the month in the afternoon in the Sinai desert; according to all that Adonoy commanded Moshe, so did Bnei Yisroel do.
They performed the Pascha, therefore, on the fourteenth day of the month, between the suns in the wilderness of Sinai; after all that the Lord had commanded Mosheh, so did the children of Israel.
9:6: There were men who were impure, having had [contact with] a corpse, and they were not able to perform the Pesach-offering on that day, and they drew near before Moshe and before Aharon, on that day.

But certain men, who were unclean, having been defiled by the body of a man who had died near them suddenly; as the commandment (of the Pascha) came upon them, could not perform it on that day, which was the seventh of their uncleanness. And they came before Mosheh and Aharon on that day;
9:7: Those men said to him: “We are impure, having had contact with a corpse; why should we be excluded and not be able to bring the offering of Adonoy in its proper time, among Bnei Yisroel?”

and these men said to him, We are unclean, on account of a man who died with us: therefore we are hindered from killing the Pascha, and shedding the blood of the Lord's oblation upon the altar at its time, that we may eat its flesh, being clean, among the children of Israel.
9:8: Moshe said to them: “Stand [wait] and I will listen to what Adonoy will instruct [command] for [regarding] you.”

This is one of four matters of judgment brought before Mosheh the prophet, which he decided according to the Word of the Holy One: in some of which Mosheh was deliberate, because they were judgments about life; but in the others Mosheh was prompt, they being (only) judgments concerning money: but in those (the former) Mosheh said, I have not heard; that he might teach the princes of the Sanhedrin who should arise after him to be deliberate in judgements regarding life, but prompt in judgments about money; and not to be ashamed to ask counsel in things too hard for them, inasmuch as Mosheh himself, the Rabbi of Israel, had need to say, I have not yet heard. Therefore, said Mosheh to them, Wait until I have heard what will be commanded from before the Lord concerning your case.
9:9: And the Lord spake with Mosheh, saying:
9:10: Speak to Bnei Yisroel, saying; any person, if he will be impure from a corpse, or [is] on a distant road, [whether among] yourselves or for your descendants, he shall perform the Pesach-offering for Adonoy

Speak with the sons of Israel, saying: A man, whether young or old, when unclean by defilement from the dead, or an issue, or the leprosy, or who is hindered in the way of the world by the accidents of the night, or who shall be at a distance from the threshold of his house: if such things happen to you, or to your generations, then may he defer to perform the Pascha before the Lord.
9:11: in the second month, on the fourteenth day in the afternoon he shall perform it. Together with matzohs and bitter herbs they shall eat it.
But in the second month, which is the month of Ijar, on the fourteenth day of the month, between the suns they shall perform it; with unleavened bread and with bitters they shall eat it.
9:12: They shall not leave any of it over until the morning and they shall not break any of its bones; according to all the statutes of the Pesach-offering they shall perform it.

They shall not leave of it till the morning, and a bone in it shall not be broken; according to every instruction in the decree of the Pascha in Nisan, they shall perform it. In the Pascha of Nisan (such persons) may eat unleavened bread, but not perform the oblation of the Pascha on account of their defilement; but in the Pascha of Ijar being purified they shall offer it.
9:13: The person who is pure and was not on the road, and refrained from performing the Pesach-offering, that soul shall be cut off from its people, for the offering of Adonoy he did not bring in its proper time; that person shall bear his sin.

But the man who, being clean and undefiled by the way of the world, and not at a distance from the threshold of his home, neglecteth to perform the oblation of the Pascha of Nisan, that man shall be cut off from his people, because he hath not offered the Lord's oblation in its season; that man shall bear his sin.
9:14: If a proselyte dwells among you and brings the Pesach-offering to Adonoy; according to the statues of the Pesach-offering and according to its laws so shall he perform it; there shall be the same statute for yourselves; [both] for the proselyte and for the native born citizen.

And if the stranger who is sojourning with you will perform the Pascha before the Lord, he shall do it after the proper manner of the Paschal decree, according to its form so shall he do it. You shall have one statute, both for the sojourner and for the native of the land.
9:15: On the day that the Mishkon was erected, the Cloud covered the Mishkon [which served] as the Tent of Testimony; and in the evening, there was over the Mishkon an appearance of fire, until morning.

And on the day on which the tabernacle was reared the Cloud of Glory covered the Tabernacle; it overspread the Tabernacle of Testimony by day, and at evening, it was over the Tabernacle like a vision of Fire until the morning.
9:16: So it always was, the Cloud covered it, and an appearance of fire, at night.
So was it continually, a Cloud of Glory covering it by day, and a vision of Fire by night.
9:17: Whenever the Cloud was lifted from the Tent, afterwards, did Bnei Yisroel travel; in the place where the Cloud came to rest, it is there that Bnei Yisroel did camp.
And what time the Cloud of Glory was uplifted from the Tabernacle, then the children of Israel went forward; and at the place where the Cloud rested, there did the children of Israel rest.
9:18: On the word of Adonoy, did Bnei Yisroel travel and on the word of Adonoy, did they camp; all those days on which the Cloud will rested above the Mishkon, did they camp.

By the mouth of the Word of the Lord the children of Israel went forward, and by the Word of the Lord they rested. All the days that the Cloud of Glory abode upon the Tabernacle, (so long) did they abide.
9:19: When the Cloud tarried above the Mishkon, for many days, Bnei Yisroel would keep the watch of [the word of] Adonoy and they would not travel.
And if the Cloud tarried over the Tabernacle many days the children of Israel observed the watch of the Word of the Lord, and did not proceed.
9:20: It sometimes happened that the Cloud was for a number of days above the Mishkon; on the order of Adonoy did they camp and on the order of Adonoy did they travel.

If for the time of a number of days, suppose the seven days of the week, the Cloud of Glory was upon the Tabernacle, by the mouth of the Word of the Lord they rested, and by the mouth of the Word of the Lord they went forward.
9:21: It sometimes happened that the Cloud was [there] [but] from evening until morning, and then the Cloud rose in the morning and they traveled; or, [the Cloud was there] for a day and a night and the Cloud was lifted, and they traveled.
Or, if the Cloud of Glory (rested only) from evening until morning, and was uplifted in the morning, then went they onward; whether by day or by night, when the Cloud was lifted up they went forward;
9:22: Or two days or a month or a year [period of time] that the Cloud prolonged its stay above the Mishkon to rest upon it; Bnei Yisroel remained encamped and they did not travel; when it rose they traveled.

whether it was two days, or a month, or a year complete, while the Cloud of Glory made stay over the Tabernacle, abiding on it, the children of Israel abode, and journeyed not, and at the time of its uplifting they went forward.
9:23: On the order of Adonoy they camped and on the order of [the word of] Adonoy they traveled; they kept the watch of Adonoy on the order of Adonoy, through Moshe.
By the mouth of the Word of the Lord they encamped, and by it they journeyed; they kept the observance of the Word of the Lord, by the mouth of the Word of the Lord through Mosheh.
10:1: And the Lord spake with Mosheh, saying:
10:2: Make for yourself two silver trumpets; you shall make them, beaten [from one block], and they shall be used by you to summon the congregation and to initiate the departure of the camps.

Make for thee, of thine, two trumpets of silver of solid material, the work of the artificer shalt thou make them; and let them be thine, with which to convoke the assembly, and for the removing of the camps.
10:3: When they will blow them, the entire congregation shall present itself to you at the entrance of the Tent of Meeting.
And thou shalt blow upon them, and bring together to thee all the congregation at the door of the tabernacle of ordinance.
10:4: But if they blow one of them, the leaders shall present themselves to you, the heads of Israel’s thousands.
If they blow upon one (only), the princes of the heads of the thousands of Israel shall assemble to thee.
10:5: When you blow a teruah [a wailing sound]; the camps that are camped eastward shall travel.
But when you blow an alarm, then the camps which are on the east are to go forward;
10:6: If you blow a second teruah, then shall travel the camps that are camped on the south side. They shall blow a teruah for their journeys.
and when they blow a second alarm, the camps on the south shall go forward; they shall blow the alarm for their journeys.
10:7: But when gathering the congregation, you shall blow [a blast], but not a teruah.
And at the time of assembling the congregation you shall blow, but not an alarm.
10:8: The sons of Aharon, the kohanim, shall sound the trumpets. This shall be for you an everlasting statute, for all your descendants.
The sons of Aharon, the priests only, shall blow with the trumpets, which shall be to you, for a perpetual statute for your generations.
10:9: If war shall come into your land against the oppresor who oppresses you and you shall blow teruahs [wail] with the trumpets and you will be remembered [your remembrance will come beneficially] before Adonoy, your God, and you will be delivered from you enemies.

And when you enter upon the order of the line of battle for your country, with oppressors who oppress you, then shall you blow the alarm on the trumpets, that the remembrance of you may come up for good before the Lord your God, that you may be delivered from your enemies.
10:10: On your joyous days and on your festivals and on the beginnings of your months you shall blow with the trumpets for your burnt-offerings and for your peace-offerings; and it shall be a remembrance for you before your God, I am Adonoy your God.

And in the day of your rejoicings, and in your solemnities, and at the beginning of your months, you shall blow with the trumpets over your burnt offerings and your consecrated victims, and they shall be for a good memorial to you before the Lord your God; for Satana shall be troubled at the sound of your jubel notes: I am the Lord your God.
10:11: It was in the second year, in the second month on the twentieth of the month that the Cloud rose up from above the Mishkon of the Testimony.
And it was in the second year, the second month, which is the month of Ijar, the twentieth day of the month, that the Cloud of Glory was uplifted from above the Tabernacle of Testimony;
10:12: Bnei Yisroel traveled along on their journeys, from the Sinai desert, and the Cloud came to rest in the desert of Paran.
and the children of Israel went forward upon their journeys from the wilderness of Sinai, and the Cloud of Glory rested in the wilderness of Pharan.
10:13: This was the first time that they traveled, on the order of Adonoy, through Moshe.
And they went forth at the first by the mouth of the Word of the Lord through Mosheh.
10:14: Then traveled the banner of the sons of Yehudah’s camp in the forefront according to their divisions; in charge of its divisions [was] Nachshon the son of Aminadav.
The standard of the camps of the Beni Jehudah went forward by their hosts, and the Rabba who was appointed over the host of the tribe of the Beni Jehudah was Nachshon bar Amminadab;
10:15: In charge of the division of the tribe of the sons of Yissachar, [was] Nesanel the son of Tzu’ar.
the Rabba of the Beni Issakar was Nethanel bar Zuar;
10:16: In charge of the division of the tribe of the sons of Zevulun, [was] Eliav the son of Cheilon.
and the Rabba of the Beni Zebulon, Eliab bar Chelon.
10:17: [Then] the Mishkon was dismantled and the sons of Gershon traveled, with the sons of Merori, those who carried the Mishkon.
And the tabernacle was taken down, and the sons of Gershon and of Merari went forward, carrying the tabernacle.
10:18: [Then] the banner of Reuven’s camp traveled, according to their divisions. In charge of its division [was] Elitzur the son of Shdeiur.
The standard of the camps of Reuben went forward by their hosts. The Rabba set over the hosts of the tribe of the Beni Reuben was Elizur bar Shedeur;
10:19: In charge of the division of the tribe of the sons of Shimon, [was] Shlumiel the son of Tzurishadai.
the Rabba of the Beni Shemeon, Shelumiel bar Zurishaddai;
10:20: In charge of the division of the tribe of the sons of Gad, [was] Elyasaf the son of De’uel.
and the Rabba of the Beni Gad, Eljasaph bar Dehuel.
10:21: [Then] the Kehos family traveled, the carriers of the sacred, and they erected the Mishkon by the time of their arrival.
And the family of Kehath went forward, carrying the sanctuary; and they (the men of Gershon) reared up the tabernacle against their coming.
10:22: [Then] the banner of the sons of Ephraim’s camp traveled according to their divisions. In charge of its division, [was] Elishamah the son of Amihud.
The standard of the camps of the Beni Ephraim went forward by their hosts: the Rabba set over the host of the tribe of Ephraim was Elishama bar Ammihud;
10:23: In charge of the division of the tribe of the sons of Menashe, [was] Gamliel the son of Pedahtzur.
the Rabba of that of Menasheh, Gamaliel bar Pedazur;
10:24: In charge of the division of the tribe of the sons of Binyamin, [was] Avidan the son of Gid’oni.
and the Rabba of Benjamin, Abidan bar Gideoni.
10:25: [Then] the banner of the sons of Don’s camp traveled; the gatherer for all the camps, according to their divisions. In charge of its division, [was] Achiezer the son of Amishadai.
And the standard of the camps of the Beni Dan went forward, completing all the camps according to their hosts; and the Rabba set over his host was Ahiezer bar Ammishaddai;
10:26: In charge of the division of the tribe of the sons of Asher, [was] Pagiel the son of Ochran.
the Rabba of the tribe of Asher, Pagiel bar Achran;
10:27: In charge of the division of the tribe of the sons of Naftali, [was] Achirah the son of Einan.
and the Rabba of the Beni Naphtali, Ahira bar Enan.
10:28: These are the journeys of Bnei Yisroel according to their divisions; and they journeyed.
These are the journeys of the children of Israel by their hosts; the Cloud of Glory was lifted up from above the tabernacle, and they went forward.
10:29: Moshe said to Chovav the son of Reuel, the Midianite, Moshe’s father-in-law: “We are journeying to the place about which Adonoy said; ‘I will give it to you’, come along with us and we will treat you well, for Adonoy spoke of bringing good [fortune] on Israel.”

And Mosheh said unto Hobab bar Reuel the Midianite, father-in-law of Mosheh, We are journeying from hence to the place of which the Lord hath said, I will give it to you: come with us, and we will do thee good; for the Lord hath spoken to do good unto the sojourner with Israel.
10:30: He said to him “I will not go, but rather to my land and to my birthplace will I go.”
But he answered him, I will not go (with you) but to my (own) land and to my kindred will I go.
10:31: He said to him “please do not forsake us, for, because you know of our encampment in the desert, and you will be our eyes [the great things that were done for us you saw with your eyes].

But he said, Do not now leave us; for when we were encamped in the wilderness, thou knewest how to judge, and didst teach us the method (or business) of judgment, and thou art dear to us as the apple of our eyes.
10:32: It will be, that when you go with us, it shall be that the very good which Adonoy will bestow on us we will bestow on (share with) you.
And it shall be that if thou wilt go on with us, with the good that the Lord shall benefit us will we benefit thee, in the division of the land.
10:33: They traveled from the mountain of Adonoy [upon which the glory of Hashem was revealed] a journey of three days, and the Ark of the Covenant of Adonoy traveled in front of them a journey of three days, to prepare for them a place to settle.

And they went forward from the mountain where the glory of the Shekinah of the Lord had been revealed, going three days; and the Ark of the Lord's covenant went before them. Thirty and six miles it went that day; it preceded the camp of Israel, going three days, to provide for them a place to encamp in.
10:34: The Cloud [of the glory] of Adonoy was above them by day when they traveled from the camp.
And the Cloud of the Lord's Shekinah overshadowed them by day in their going out from the encampment.
10:35: Whenever the Ark departed Moshe woud say: “Rise, [reveal Yourself] Adonoy, and may Your enemies disperse, and those who hate You flee before You.”

And it was when the ark should go forward, the Cloud gathered itself together and stood still, not going on, until Mosheh, standing in prayer, prayed and supplicated mercy from before the Lord, and thus spake: Let the Word of the Lord be now revealed in the power of Thy anger, that the adversaries of Thy people may be scattered; and let not the banner of those who hate them be uplifted before Thee.
10:36: When it rested, he would say: “Come to rest, Adonoy, [dwell in Your glory] among the myriads and thousands of Israel.”

But when the ark should rest, the Cloud gathered itself to ether and stood, but did not overspread, until Mosheh, standing in prayer, prayed and besought mercy from before the Lord, thus speaking: Return now, Thou Word of the Lord, in the goodness of Thy mercy, and lead Thy people Israel, and let the glory of Thy Shekinah dwell among them, and (Thy) mercy with the myriads of the house of Jakob, and with the multitudes of the thousands of Israel.
